name: HC-06 Bluetooth serial module (slave)
description: Classic Bluetooth 2.0 serial-port (SPP) slave module (CSR BC417, linvor firmware): a phone or PC pairs with it (name linvor or HC-06, PIN 1234) and the bytes it sends appear on the module's UART, and back. Default 9600 8N1; while nothing is connected it answers a few AT commands (no line ending, one per second). Supply 3.6-6 V into the board's 3.3 V regulator; RXD/TXD are 3.3 V logic. Sold as: HC-06 4-pin slave module on the blue JY-MCU-style backplate (header VCC, GND, TXD, RXD; no button), the common clone sold by most hobby shops.
eli5: Lets your phone send messages to your board over Bluetooth, like an invisible serial cable.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply 3.6-6 V into the board's 3.3 V regulator (use 5 V, not 3.3 V)

pins.name: TXD
pins.description: Module's UART output (3.3 V). Wire to the microcontroller's RX

pins.name: RXD
pins.description: Module's UART input, 3.3 V logic only. Wire to the microcontroller's TX (1k/2k divider from a 5 V board)

supplierQuery: HC-06 Bluetooth serial module slave 4 pin
buildNotes: Power VCC from 5 V (VIN/VBUS): the backplate's regulator needs at least 3.6 V.
Cross the serial lines: module TXD to the board's RX, module RXD to the board's TX. RXD is 3.3 V only; from a 5 V Arduino use a 1k/2k divider.
Factory settings: 9600 8N1, name linvor (newer firmware: HC-06), PIN 1234. It is slave only: the phone or PC starts the connection.
AT commands work only while nothing is connected (LED blinking). Send them in capitals with NO \r\n and at most one per second: the module ends a command by the pause after it.
Replies have no line ending either: AT -> OK, AT+VERSION -> OKlinvorV1.8, AT+NAMExxx -> OKsetname, AT+PINxxxx -> OKsetPIN, AT+BAUD4 -> OK9600. Settings survive power-off.
Once a phone connects (LED steady) every byte is passed straight through; AT commands are not answered.

example.code:
from machine import UART, Pin
import time
from hc06 import HC06

# No phone connected yet, so the HC-06 answers AT commands (9600 baud, no line ending).
u = UART({UART_ID}, baudrate=9600, tx=Pin({RXD}), rx=Pin({TXD}))
bt = HC06(u)
try:
    bt.ping()
    print('HC-06 %s' % bt.version())
except OSError as e:
    print(e)
print('Waiting for the phone')
while True:
    line = bt.readline()
    if line:
        print('PHONE SENT %s' % line)
        bt.write(b'got ' + line.encode() + b'\r\n')
    time.sleep_ms(20)

test.title: Answers AT with its firmware version, then prints what the connected phone sends
